summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for an upper gastrointestinal bleed. He presented with blood in his stool for four days, fatigue, dizziness, and new dyspnea. His hematocrit dropped from 33.9 to 22.6, requiring three units of packed red blood cells. An upper endoscopy revealed severe esophagitis and mild duodenitis as the likely source of bleeding. He was treated with high-dose IV pantoprazole, transitioned to oral omeprazole 40 mg twice daily, and advised to avoid NSAIDs. He developed transient non-sustained ventricular tachycardia due to hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia, which resolved with repletion. Pulmonary edema was managed with dialysis and medication adjustments. Atrial fibrillation was controlled with diltiazem. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned with GI, transplant surgery for graft pain evaluation, and his primary care provider.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
Diaphragmatic hernia without mention of obstruction or gangrene
